newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Yet again, Taiwan stocks close at 22-month high.
newsitem.headline: Yet again, Taiwan stocks close at 22-month high.

text.p: Waves of buying in conglomerate and plastics shares pushed Taiwan share prices to yet another 22-month high on Saturday, but brokers warned that heavy selling pressure next week could cap the recent bull run.
The weighted index ended 80.77 points or 1.19 percent higher at 6,842.16, its highest finish since January 9, 1995, but back somewhat from a bullish intra-session high of 6,856.39.
Prices hit 22-month highs all but one day this week. At a hectic T$103 billion, turnover nearly bested Friday's T$105 billion despite the abbreviated two-hour Saturday session.
Plastics were the day's top gainers, surging 3.55 percent.
"Bullish buying in conglomerate shares such as the Formosa group led the market to surpass the 6,800-point barrier," said Tank Hung, an analyst of Yuan Ta Securities.
Nan Ya Plastics, a key Formosa Plastics group member, jumped T$4 or 6.84 percent to T$62.5. Shipping giant Evergreen Marine soared the daily seven percent limit, up T$3.5 to T$53.5.
Electronics shares gained 1.12 percent but Hung cautioned that the sector's recent hot streak may be cooling.
"Buying in electronics is slowing and some people are starting to switch interest to blue-chip conglomerate shares from electronics," he said.
"It may be time for electronics to consolidate," Hung added.
Brokers expected the index to continue its uptrend next week, but said the gains were likely to be limited.
A 6,700-6,900 trading range was seen for next week.
